claim: Over the alphabet \(\Sigma=\{a,b,c\}\), the length-three word \(\mathtt{abc}\) has probabilistic automatic complexity \(A_P(\mathtt{abc},\Sigma)=2\). The rational two-state PFA with initial distribution \((1/3,2/3)\), accepting state \(A\), and letter updates \(p\mapsto 1/2+p/6\), \(p\mapsto 1/2-p/2\), and \(p\mapsto 1-2p/3\) for \(a,b,c\), respectively, gives \(\rho(\mathtt{abc})=47/54\) while every other length-three word has acceptance probability at most \(23/27\); the exact gap is \(1/54\).
integrity: All 27 length-three words were checked by exact rational recurrence using the embedded standalone verification script; no external or independent certification is claimed.
scientific_limitations: The result is a minimal length-three ternary example, not a classification for longer words or larger alphabets.
The exact gap \(1/54\) is for the displayed rational PFA and is not claimed optimal.
title: A minimal ternary witness for two-state probabilistic automatic complexity
